transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um, well, what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I just keep getting up during things where I really, really know I should stay put. 

Like during our sprint planning meetings at work—I'm a software developer, and honestly our current project is such a mess right now because the client keeps changing the requirements every two days, which completely defeats the purpose of having a sprint in the first place, you know? It drives my manager absolutely crazy, and the whole team is just exhausted. But anyway, during those meetings, or even during these super important mortgage calls I've been having... we're trying to buy a new place, and the housing market is just absolutely wild right now. We saw this one house last weekend that smelled completely like wet dog and they still wanted twenty percent over asking, which is just ridiculous for the square footage... 

Wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the calls. So I'll be on these calls and I just... get up. Like I'll suddenly decide I need a glass of water right that exact second, or I'll just get up and decide to check something in the other room when I know I'm supposed to be sitting there and paying attention.
Do you feel anxious or nervous before these meetings or calls where you end up getting up and leaving?

No, I wouldn't say I'm anxious. I don't dread them or get nervous or anything like that. Like, with the mortgage calls, our broker is actually this really nice guy named Greg. He's always wearing these wildly patterned ties on Zoom, which is funny because he works from home, so he's probably wearing sweatpants on the bottom, you know? 

My husband does that all the time now. Just the other day the Amazon guy rang the bell and my husband answered the door in a crisp button-down shirt and these bright red plaid pajama pants... the delivery guy looked so confused. It was hilarious. We get so many packages now because we keep buying stuff for the new house even though we haven't even closed on one yet. 

But um... what were we saying? Oh, right, nerves. No, I'm not nervous before they start. I just... suddenly have to move once I'm actually in them.
Do you find it hard to focus on what's being discussed during those meetings or calls before you get up and leave?

Um, yeah, I guess I do. Like, I'll sit down and start reviewing a pull request for work, or, you know, reading through all those massive mortgage documents Greg sends over. And I always start with really good intentions! I'm like, okay, let's just get this done. 

But... well, especially with the pull requests. We have this one junior developer on the team, Kevin, and he never, ever leaves comments on his code. And he uses spaces instead of tabs, which is a whole massive debate in the programming world, I know, but it honestly just looks terrible on my screen. I actually just bought one of those curved ultrawide monitors to try and help my home office setup, and it takes up my entire desk. The stand is ridiculously huge. I had to move my favorite succulent to the windowsill just to make it fit, and now I think it's getting too much direct sunlight because the leaves are getting a little crispy... 

Wait, sorry. Focus. Right. So, yeah, I'll start looking at Kevin's code or reading the mortgage paperwork, and after just a few minutes I'll suddenly realize I've been staring at the exact same section of text for I don't know how long, and I'm not actually processing a single word of it. My brain is just off thinking about five completely unrelated things at once, like the crispy plant or what we're having for dinner. And then that's usually when I just feel like I have to get up.
Do you feel like you're making a conscious decision to get up and leave during those meetings or calls, or is it more like you just find yourself getting up without thinking about it?

Um, I think it's more like... I just find myself doing it? Like, it's not a conscious choice where I sit there and weigh the pros and cons of standing up. It's just like, boom, I'm up. 

Actually, it kind of reminds me of my cat, Barnaby. He's this massive orange tabby we adopted last year. He has this thing where he'll be totally dead asleep on the couch, just completely out cold, and then suddenly he'll bolt upright and sprint across the room like he's chasing something invisible. We call them the zoomies, but it's so weird because there's literally nothing there. My husband thinks we have a ghost or something, but I read somewhere that cats just have these bursts of pent-up energy they need to release. Which makes sense, because he's an indoor cat, and we bought him all these expensive toys—like this little motorized mouse that squeaks—and he completely ignores them. He'd rather play with a crumpled up receipt from the grocery store. 

Wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, making a decision to get up. Yeah, no, I don't think about it. I just... I'm just suddenly out of my chair.
Do you feel like getting up during those meetings or calls helps you feel more focused or calm afterwards?

Um, focused or calm? No, not really. I mean, getting up doesn't really fix the... the feeling. It's like, even when I'm sitting down and I look completely still on the outside, inside I just have this intense pressure. Like I need to be moving, or switching tasks, or just doing something with my hands, otherwise I feel like I'm going to crawl right out of my skin. 

It's actually why I started knitting a few years ago. I thought having something to do with my hands would help. I bought all this really expensive merino wool yarn online—it was dyed by hand in this little shop in Vermont. The colors were gorgeous, like deep sea greens and blues. I was going to make this beautiful cable-knit sweater for my husband. I watched all these YouTube tutorials on how to do the specific stitches, and the woman in the video had the most soothing voice, almost like an ASMR thing. I ended up falling down this huge rabbit hole of watching soap-cutting videos because they popped up in the recommendations, and before I knew it, it was 2 AM and I hadn't even cast on the first row of the sweater. 

Anyway, the yarn is still sitting in a basket in our living room. My cat Barnaby loves sleeping on it, which means it's covered in orange hair now, so I probably couldn't even use it if I wanted to. But um... yeah, no, getting up doesn't really make me feel calm. The restless feeling is just kind of always there, bubbling under the surface.
Do you often act on impulse without fully thinking through the consequences?

Um, act on impulse? I don't... I don't really know if I do that. Like, I don't think I do things without thinking about the consequences, but maybe? I'm not really sure what you mean by that. 

Like, the other day I was at the grocery store, just trying to get some almond milk. Greg and I have been trying to cut back on dairy because we watched this documentary on Netflix about the dairy industry. It was so intense, honestly. They had all these hidden cameras and everything. But anyway, I was in the alternative milk aisle, which by the way is huge now. They have oat, soy, macadamia, even pistachio milk! Who knew you could milk a pistachio? I actually bought a bag of pistachios once to try making it myself because I saw a TikTok about it. You have to soak them overnight and then blend them, but I forgot they were soaking and they got all weird and mushy, so I just threw them out. 

But um, what were we talking about? Consequences? Yeah, I don't know if I really act on impulse like that. I just... I don't think I've really noticed doing that.
Do you have trouble paying attention or following through on instructions in situations where you're not feeling the need to get up or move around?

Um, paying attention when I don't need to move? Yeah, I definitely struggle with that. It's like, I can sit down to review a pull request at work, or even something important at home, like... oh, Greg and I are looking at refinancing our house, so we have all these mortgage documents. And I'll sit down with the best intentions, you know? I'll have my coffee, my highlighters—I bought this pack of pastel highlighters that are supposed to be easier on the eyes, because regular neon yellow just gives me a headache after a while. I actually read an article about how certain colors can affect your productivity, and blue is supposed to be the best for focus. So I painted my home office this really nice shade of slate blue, but it ended up looking kind of gray in the afternoon light, which was a little disappointing. We got the paint from this local hardware store where the owner has a golden retriever that just sleeps by the register all day. He's so sweet, I always end up petting him for like ten minutes when I go in there. 

But um, wait, the documents. Right. So I'll sit down to read them, and after a few minutes, I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same paragraph. My eyes are looking at the words, but my brain is completely somewhere else. Like, I'll be thinking about the grocery list, or whether I remembered to feed Barnaby, or what I'm going to make for dinner, or that weird dream I had last night about being on a boat. It's just... five different unrelated things going on at once, and I haven't actually absorbed a single word of what I'm supposed to be reading.
Do you have trouble organizing your daily tasks or managing your time effectively?

Um, organizing tasks? Yeah, it's... it's kind of a mess, honestly. Like, I have my work tickets, notes about fixing things around the house, reminders about the budget... and they're just everywhere. Some are in Slack, some are on sticky notes, some are in my email, and a bunch are on my phone. I actually just got a new phone case because my old one was cracking at the corners. It's this really pretty sage green color with little daisies on it. I found it on Etsy from this seller who makes them out of recycled ocean plastic, which I thought was really cool. Greg and I have been trying to be more eco-friendly lately, like with the almond milk thing, and we even started composting. Though the compost bin in the kitchen started attracting fruit flies, so I had to make this little trap out of apple cider vinegar and dish soap. It actually worked really well! 

But um, yeah, because my notes are scattered all over the place, I end up spending way more time just trying to figure out what I was supposed to be doing in the first place, rather than actually getting anything done. It's really frustrating.
Have you noticed any difficulties in your relationships with family or friends due to your tendency to get up and leave during meetings or calls?

Um, leaving during calls? Well, not exactly the leaving part, but just... the whole scattered thing. It's definitely starting to create some friction, yeah. Like at work, and with Greg at home. People are having to follow up with me way more than they used to. Actually, my manager, Sarah, she just got this new standing desk because she read that sitting all day is basically the new smoking. I tried a standing desk once, but I just ended up shifting my weight from one foot to the other constantly, and then my knees started hurting. I think I need better shoes if I'm going to do that, maybe those ones with the really thick foam soles? I saw an ad for them on Instagram the other day, but they were like hundred and fifty dollars, which seems like a lot for sneakers. 

But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, the friction. Yeah, people have to keep reminding me about things, and I really worry that I'm becoming the unreliable one. Especially when it comes to planning tasks or organizing things. And the thing is, I'm trying really hard! I'm not doing it on purpose, but it just feels like I'm letting people down.
Do you feel upset or overwhelmed when you're unable to focus or complete a task?

Um, overwhelmed? Yeah, I mean... I do get frustrated, but I wouldn't say I get super upset or overwhelmed. It's more just like a sigh, you know? Like, "here we go again." I guess I've just gotten kind of used to it. Like when I was trying to organize my spice rack last weekend. I bought all these matching glass jars with those little bamboo lids, because our old plastic ones were getting all sticky. I saw this whole organization video on TikTok where this woman made custom vinyl labels for every single spice, even the really obscure ones like sumac and cardamom. I don't even know what you use sumac for, to be honest. I think maybe Mediterranean food? Greg loves Greek food, we actually went to this amazing little place downtown for our anniversary last year that had the best tzatziki I've ever tasted. It was so garlicky, which I love, but then you kind of have to make sure both of you eat it, right? Otherwise, the car ride home is just... well. 

But um, yeah, no, I don't really get super overwhelmed by it. It's annoying, definitely, but I just kind of roll with it at this point.
Have you ever done something impulsively that you later regretted?

Um, impulsively? Like doing something I regret... I don't really think so. I mean, I guess I make quick decisions sometimes, but nothing that I look back on and think, "Oh wow, that was a terrible idea." Well, actually, there was this one time I decided to cut my own bangs. Have you ever done that? It was during that weird phase a few years ago when everyone was trying to learn how to bake sourdough bread and cut their own hair. I watched this YouTube tutorial by this girl who made it look so easy. She had this really cool aesthetic, like her whole apartment was filled with monsteras and pothos plants. I actually bought a monstera after watching that video, but I think I overwatered it because the leaves started turning yellow and getting these weird brown spots. I read that you're supposed to let the top two inches of soil dry out before you water them again, but I always forget to check. I even bought one of those little moisture meters you stick in the dirt, but I lost it. I think it might be in the drawer with the batteries and the superglue. 

But um, yeah, the bangs were a disaster, obviously. But I wouldn't say I do impulsive things that I really regret in a serious way. Just, you know, normal silly stuff like the hair thing. Nothing major.
Do you have trouble controlling your emotions when you're feeling restless or frustrated?

Um, controlling my emotions? Not really, no. I mean, I definitely feel the restlessness, like I'm a motor that won't shut off, but I don't snap at people or anything. I just kind of keep it moving. Literally, sometimes. Like when I'm debugging code and I just can't find the syntax error. I'll just get up and start pacing around my home office. We actually just painted that room, by the way. Greg wanted this deep navy blue, but I thought it would make the room look too small, especially since the window only gets morning light. We ended up compromising on this really nice sage green. It's called "Quiet Willow" or something like that. We got it from that hardware store on 4th Street, the one with the really old creaky wooden floors? I love the smell of that place, it smells like sawdust and... I don't know, productivity? I actually bought a new hammer while we were there because I couldn't find my old one. I think I left it at my sister's house when I helped her hang those floating shelves in her bathroom. She has this tiny little half-bath that she's trying to make look like a spa, with all these eucalyptus bundles hanging in the shower. 

But um, what was the question? Oh, emotions. Yeah, no, I don't really lose control of my emotions when I'm frustrated. I just get kind of fidgety and need to move around, but I don't get angry or anything like that.
Do you often find yourself saying or doing things without thinking them through?

Um, doing things without thinking? Well, I guess talking without thinking happens a lot. Like at work, I catch myself answering my teammates before they've even finished explaining a bug or asking their question. And sometimes I'm already talking when I realize I totally guessed wrong about where they were going with it. It's just so hard to wait when I think I know the answer! Speaking of work, we're actually switching over to a whole new project management software next month. They've had us doing these mandatory training modules, which are just incredibly dry. The guy doing the voiceover for the videos sounds exactly like that actor from those old allergy medicine commercials. You know the ones? Where the people are walking through a field of daisies and everything looks kind of hazy and yellow? I always wondered if they actually filmed those in real fields or if it was just a green screen. I'm pretty sure it's green screen now, CGI has gotten so good. I was watching this behind-the-scenes documentary about how they made the new superhero movie, and it's wild how much is just people in gray suits with little ping pong balls attached to them. 

But um, yeah, I definitely jump the gun when people are talking to me. I just blurt things out before they finish their sentence.
Did you have any behavioral problems when you were a kid, like getting into trouble at school or having difficulty following rules?

Um, behavioral problems? Well, not like getting sent to the principal's office for fighting or anything bad like that. But I definitely got in trouble for, like, being disruptive, I guess? I remember in elementary school, my teachers were always having to move my desk. Like, they'd put me right next to the teacher's desk, or in the back corner, because I was just always popping out of my seat. Or I'd just start talking before they called on me. And I'd rush through all my worksheets even if I actually knew how to do the math or whatever. I just wanted to be done. 

Which reminds me, my niece is in third grade now, and they do math so differently! Have you seen this "new math" they teach? My sister was showing me her homework the other day, and they have to draw all these boxes and grids just to multiply two numbers. It took me like ten minutes to figure out what the worksheet was even asking her to do. I mean, I write code for a living, and I was stumped by eight-year-old math. We ended up just making a game out of it with these little colorful counting blocks she has. They were shaped like little dinosaurs. I actually used to have a huge collection of those plastic dinosaurs when I was her age. I kept them in this old metal Band-Aid tin. Remember when Band-Aids used to come in those tin boxes instead of cardboard? I kind of miss those. They were so useful for storing little things. 

But um, yeah, back to school. I wasn't a bad kid, just... you know, always jumping up and talking out of turn and rushing through my work. They were always telling me to just sit down and wait.
Did you have a lot of energy as a child, like you were always running, climbing, or couldn't sit still?

Um, energy as a kid? Yeah, definitely. I was always climbing on the furniture and stuff. But honestly, it's like that energy never really went away, it just kind of... went internal? Like, even now, even when I’m sitting calmly on the outside, I feel this intense pressure inside like I need to move, switch tasks, or just do something with my hands before I crawl out of my skin. 

That's actually why I got into building mechanical keyboards. Have you ever tried one? I use the tactile switches because it gives my hands that physical feedback I need without being obnoxiously loud on Zoom calls. My coworker Dave uses these super clicky blue switches and it sounds like a typewriter falling down a flight of stairs whenever we pair-program. It's so loud. But anyway, I just ordered a new set of keycaps for my main board. They're this really cool retro 80s colorway, like neon pink and teal. But the shipping got totally delayed because of that huge storm up north last week. My regular mail carrier, Gary, was telling me their whole distribution center is still backed up. Gary's great, he always brings a treat for my neighbor's golden retriever. That dog is so funny, he literally waits by the fence every day at exactly 2 PM. I'd love to get a dog, but my HOA has this weird rule where you can't have pets over 20 pounds. Which is just strange, right? Like, what if you have a really fat cat? Do they come around and weigh the cat? 

But um, what was the question again? Oh, right, sitting still. Yeah, so even if I look like I'm sitting perfectly still, inside I'm just vibrating and feeling that pressure to do something.
Have you experienced these feelings of restlessness and difficulty sitting still for as long as you can remember, even as a young child?

Um, for as long as I can remember? Well, I mean, the energy was always there, like I said. But honestly, this feeling of it being so internal and hard to manage? That's really spiked more recently. It's been noticeably harder to manage for about two years, basically since we took on the mortgage and had to deal with all the extra paperwork and planning that came with buying the house. 

The amount of paper they make you sign for a mortgage is just unbelievable. The notary actually came to our old apartment for the closing, and she had this giant stack of documents. And she was so strict about me using blue ink. She said it was to prove it wasn't a photocopy, which makes sense, I guess. But I'm kind of a pen snob—I guess it goes with the mechanical keyboard thing, I just like nice tactile tools. Anyway, she handed me this incredibly cheap, scratchy ballpoint pen to sign like a hundred pages. I usually use fountain pens. I have this really beautiful Japanese one with a gold nib that writes like absolute butter. I even import my ink because the colors are just so much richer than what you can buy here. I have this one shade, it's called Yama-budo, and it's this gorgeous deep crushed grape color. I actually spilled half a bottle of it on my desk mat a few weeks ago and it looked like an absolute crime scene. I tried everything to get it out—baking soda, club soda, even that special carpet cleaner my mom swears by. My mom actually uses that cleaner on everything, she buys it in bulk at Costco. Have you ever been to a Costco on a Saturday morning? It's like a gladiator arena just trying to get a parking spot. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, so definitely the last two years with the mortgage and all that planning, that's when the restlessness got really tough to manage.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you, even when you're trying to focus on something?

Um, distracted? I don't... I don't really think so. Not more than anyone else, I mean. Like, if I'm in the zone writing code, I'm pretty locked in. Though, to be fair, my home office looks out over the street, and sometimes I'll catch myself watching the garbage truck. They just switched to those automated ones with the giant robotic arm that grabs the bins? It's fascinating to watch. The driver just sits in there with a joystick like he's playing an arcade game. I used to love arcade games when I was in college. There was this place near campus that had all the classic cabinets—Pac-Man, Galaga, Donkey Kong. We'd go there on Thursday nights because they had two-for-one token deals and cheap pizza. The pizza was terrible, honestly, like cardboard with ketchup on it, but when you're 20 and broke, you don't really care. I actually tried making homemade pizza last weekend with one of those baking steels. You're supposed to preheat it for like an hour so it gets super hot and crisps the crust. It kind of worked, but I put way too much mozzarella on it and it got all soupy in the middle. The cheese completely slid off the first slice I picked up. 

But um, yeah, distracted. No, I don't really notice being easily distracted by stuff around me when I'm trying to focus.
Do you experience these feelings of restlessness and difficulty sitting still in most areas of your life, such as at work, at home, and in social situations?

Um, in most areas of my life? Yeah, I guess so. It's definitely creating some friction lately, especially at work and at home. Like, people are having to follow up with me way more than they used to, and I'm really starting to worry that I'm becoming the unreliable one for planning things, even though I'm honestly trying so hard. 

It's just... I'll be in a meeting, or trying to sort out our weekend plans with my husband, and I just have this overwhelming urge to get up and pace. Which reminds me, we were supposed to go to this new farmer's market last weekend. It's in that big empty lot behind the old movie theater? They finally tore that theater down, by the way. It's kind of sad, I saw the first Lord of the Rings movie there. The seats were terribly uncomfortable, but the popcorn was amazing. They used real butter, not that weird yellow oil stuff. I actually bought a popcorn machine for the house a few months ago, one of those retro-looking ones with the glass sides? It's huge. I didn't realize how big it was when I ordered it online, and now it just takes up half the counter space in the kitchen. My husband hates it, but he loves the popcorn, so he can't complain too much. We got this special seasoning salt for it that tastes exactly like movie theater popcorn. It comes in this tiny shaker, but it lasts forever. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the restlessness. Yeah, it's definitely happening everywhere—work, home, social stuff. It's just making planning and keeping track of things a lot harder lately, and I hate feeling like I'm dropping the ball when people are counting on me.

Have you experienced significant difficulties in your daily life, such as problems at work, in relationships, or with completing tasks, as a result of your restlessness and difficulty staying focused?

Um, significant difficulties? Yeah, like I was just saying, it's really starting to create some friction for me. At work, and at home too. People are having to follow up with me way more than they used to, just to make sure I'm actually getting things done. And I really worry that I'm becoming the unreliable one, especially when it comes to planning tasks. I mean, I'm trying so hard, I really am. I even bought this special planner to try and keep everything straight. It's one of those bullet journals, you know? Where you have to draw out all the calendars and lists yourself. 

I thought it would help because I could customize it, but I spent like three hours just picking out the right kind of washi tape to decorate the edges of the pages. Have you ever looked into washi tape? There are literally thousands of patterns. I found this one Etsy shop based in Kyoto that makes tape with tiny metallic gold foil constellations on it. It took three weeks to ship, and when it finally arrived, the mail carrier left it out in the rain because our porch awning is leaking. We really need to get that fixed. The handyman we usually call retired last year and moved to Florida. He sends us a Christmas card every year with his two golden retrievers on it. They're such beautiful dogs. I grew up with a golden retriever named Barnaby, he used to eat the remote control if we didn't hide it... 

But wait, sorry, what did you ask? Oh, right, problems in daily life. Yeah, it's just the friction, you know? Having people follow up with me constantly and feeling like I can't be trusted with planning things anymore. It's really frustrating.
Have you ever been diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder or does anyone in your family have it?

Um, diagnosed? No, never. And my family... I don't think so? I mean, my dad is always bouncing around his garage tinkering with things, but he's a retired mechanical engineer, so that's just kind of his personality. He actually built this incredible birdhouse out of scrap wood last summer. It's like an exact replica of a Victorian mansion, complete with a tiny wraparound porch. He even hand-painted individual little shingles on the roof. It took him weeks to finish it. 

I actually tried taking up painting a few years ago because of him. I signed up for a watercolor class at the community center downtown. The instructor was this really eccentric lady who always wore these massive, brightly colored silk scarves. She told us she bought them all at a flea market in Paris when she was backpacking through Europe in her twenties. I've always wanted to go to Paris, honestly, mostly just to eat the pastries. I follow this French baker on Instagram who makes these croissants that are perfectly geometric, they look almost too good to eat. I tried making croissants from scratch once, but the butter got too warm and leaked all over the baking sheet, and it set off the smoke detector. Our smoke detector is incredibly sensitive, if you even look at the toaster wrong it starts blaring...

But, um... wait, sorry. What were you asking about my family? Oh, right, a diagnosis. No, no one has ever been diagnosed with anything like that, as far as I know.

patient.answer:
Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um, well, what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I just keep getting up during things where I really, really know I should stay put. 

Like during our sprint planning meetings at work—I'm a software developer, and honestly our current project is such a mess right now because the client keeps changing the requirements every two days, which completely defeats the purpose of having a sprint in the first place, you know? It drives my manager absolutely crazy, and the whole team is just exhausted. But anyway, during those meetings, or even during these super important mortgage calls I've been having... we're trying to buy a new place, and the housing market is just absolutely wild right now. We saw this one house last weekend that smelled completely like wet dog and they still wanted twenty percent over asking, which is just ridiculous for the square footage... 

Wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the calls. So I'll be on these calls and I just... get up. Like I'll suddenly decide I need a glass of water right that exact second, or I'll just get up and decide to check something in the other room when I know I'm supposed to be sitting there and paying attention.

patient.answer:
No, I wouldn't say I'm anxious. I don't dread them or get nervous or anything like that. Like, with the mortgage calls, our broker is actually this really nice guy named Greg. He's always wearing these wildly patterned ties on Zoom, which is funny because he works from home, so he's probably wearing sweatpants on the bottom, you know?

It was hilarious. We get so many packages now because we keep buying stuff for the new house even though we haven't even closed on one yet. 

But um... what were we saying? Oh, right, nerves. No, I'm not nervous before they start. I just... suddenly have to move once I'm actually in them.

I actually tried taking up painting a few years ago because of him. I signed up for a watercolor class at the community center downtown. The instructor was this really eccentric lady who always wore these massive, brightly colored silk scarves. She told us she bought them all at a flea market in Paris when she was backpacking through Europe in her twenties. I've always wanted to go to Paris, honestly, mostly just to eat the pastries. I follow this French baker on Instagram who makes these croissants that are perfectly geometric, they look almost too good to eat. I tried making croissants from scratch once, but the butter got too warm and leaked all over the baking sheet, and it set off the smoke detector. Our smoke detector is incredibly sensitive, if you even look at the toaster wrong it starts blaring...

But, um... wait, sorry. What were you asking about my family? Oh, right, a diagnosis. No, no one has ever been diagnosed with anything like that, as far as I know.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of restlessness, difficulty staying focused, and impulsive behaviors are consistent with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), predominantly hyperactive-impulsive type.
